bullets.title: Fed hike risk rising: Sept CPI could push odds to 70%
bullets.body: September Fed hike odds sit at ~62% and could reach 70% if Core PCE prints 0.3% m/m; December 2027 Fed funds expected near 4.25%. Atlanta Fed GDPNow tracking 3Q26 real GDP at 4.74%, with consumer spending needing to slow from 2.5–3% to ~2%. Treasury yields near cycle highs with 10-year risk range at 4.70–4.87% per Hedgeye.

bullets.title: Hedgeye flips net short equities (2L/6S); long oil, short duration
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough moved from 12L/1S to 2L/6S as S&P 500 hit a lower high from the top of its risk range; immediate-term S&P range 7,615–7,772. Remaining longs are consumer staples (SJM named). Short TLT, ZROZ, XLU, LQD on yield acceleration thesis; estimates $1 oil increase = 3–4 bps CPI, with WTI move from $87 to $94 potentially pushing CPI to 3.7–3.8%.

bullets.title: Oil breakout at $92 WTI; energy sector outperforming on supply disruption bets, not fundamentals
bullets.body: WTI broke above $92 (+1.2% in pre-market) with Hedgeye's medium-term target toward $96 amid Middle East supply concerns; EIA forecasts 0.6Mb/d disruption through end of 2027. Quant analysis notes energy had the weakest EPS beat rates of any sector YTD yet led YTD performance — outperformance is expectation- and inflation-protection-driven, not fundamental. XLE technical target cited at 73.

bullets.title: MS 'Age of Inference': rotate from semis/hardware into hyperscalers + power infra
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgrades AI cycle framing to 'Age of Inference,' preferring Compute > Networking > Memory. Hyperscaler capex grows ~60% to ~$550B in 2027 then decelerates to ~12% in 2028 — the key rotation trigger. ASICs rising from 34% to 66% of incremental capacity by 2028 creates structural long-term NVDA share risk; META achieves highest ROIC (~46%) among infra models. NVDA OW PT $300 (+30%), META OW PT $775 (+26%), MSFT OW PT $600 (+20%), AMZN OW PT $335 (+30%).

bullets.title: GS TMT: semis 'most loved'; software sentiment muted; 'inference economy' plays expanding multiples
bullets.body: At the GS Communacopia + Technology Conference, semis remain the most-loved group but semicap multiples are compressed as investors debate whether CY27 upside is 'known.' Software sentiment is muted — investors await tangible revenue revisions to validate SaaS AI integration. 'Inference economy' plays (SNOW, TWLO) are showing meaningful multiple expansion as perceived more immune to capex gyrations. AI adoption by US firms at 22.4%, expected to rise to 25.9% in 6 months per Census Bureau.

bullets.title: HF positioning: rotating fastest into Quality/hyperscalers since 'Liberation Day'; semis short at 60th %tile
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley PB reports hedge funds broadening into high-quality TMT (hyperscalers) at the fastest clip since mid-2025. HF net positioning to the long leg of the Quality factor is only at the 14th percentile vs. last decade, suggesting room to run. Semis short exposure pushed to 60th percentile; SaaS shorts fallen to 15th percentile. US L/S funds up >10% YTD with net leverage at 54% and gross leverage near 12-month lows.

bullets.title: Momentum extremes and sentiment reset create potential violent reversal setup
bullets.body: JPMorgan flags momentum at the 5th percentile and broadest equity sentiment collapsed from the 99th to 10th percentile — a setup that has historically preceded violent reversals. Semis/AI winners underperformed software/AI losers by the most since the 2009 quant unwind. HFs re-grossed last week at a +1.3z clip; KOSPI up ~4% led by memory/tech.

bullets.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra launch catalyzes broad semi outperformance; ADBE under pressure
bullets.body: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra release, featuring step-up in complex reasoning and agentic workloads, drove broad semiconductor outperformance in pre-market. Oracle and SoftBank flagged as major beneficiaries; ASML boosted by key commitments to High-NA EUV for HVM and 12-inch photomask shift. ADBE under pressure as Astra raises CAD software/EDA disruption fears; SNPS upgraded Overweight at Morgan Stanley.

bullets.title: AI capex Asia checks: 70K NVL racks, TPUs doubling; supply chasing demand across the stack
bullets.body: Oppenheimer Asia checks show NVL rack volumes tracking ~70K in 2026 (vs. ~50K prior), with TPU units expected to roughly double to 7–8M next year. Wafer/CoWoS allocation increasingly favors scaled players NVDA and AVGO as a 'competitive weapon.' Supply constraints span wafers, CoWoS, HBM, CPUs, and substrates — advanced packaging stretched up to 9 months. CSPs expected to drive $1.3T capex next year, up >50%. Consumer (handset/PC) remains the weak spot with handsets down ~20% in China.

bullets.title: NVDA acquiring Hugging Face for $12.9B; VRT buying UtilityInnovation Group for $2.6B
bullets.body: Weekly M&A digest: NVIDIA confirms agreement to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9B including a $1B retention package. Vertiv to acquire UtilityInnovation Group for ~$1.45B cash plus up to ~$1.15B contingent consideration. Aon confirmed acquisition of USI Insurance Services from KKR for $17.0B.

bullets.title: Qualcomm-Amazon multi-gen AI data center collaboration; 25M-share warrant issued
bullets.body: Qualcomm announced a multi-generation collaboration with Amazon to develop customized AI inference silicon for large-scale data centers, plus optical connectivity solutions up to 1.6T capacity. As part of the deal, Qualcomm issued a 25M-share warrant to Amazon at $161.26/sh (expires 2036), with shares vesting tied to up to $60B in Amazon purchases. Qualcomm also expanding use of Amazon Bedrock for EDA workloads to reduce chip design cycles.

bullets.title: 52-week high/low breadth: energy minerals and transports leading highs; tech services and consumer at lows
bullets.body: StreetAccount flags 52 stocks hitting 52-week highs vs. 29 at lows. Energy Minerals led with 8 highs/0 lows; VLO, MPC, PSX each up 2–3%. Technology Services showed 1 high vs. 4 lows; Electronic Technology 0 highs vs. 3 lows. Consumer Non-Durables had the most 52-week lows with 5 names.

bullets.title: VIX +5.7% to 15.36; SaaS and enterprise software names weak in pre-market
bullets.body: VIX rose 5.7% to 15.36 with broad-based options activity across 25+ names. Pre-market weakness concentrated in SaaS/enterprise software: TEAM -2.3%, SHOP -2.2%, WDAY -1.9%, NOW -1.8%, TWLO -2.1%, DOCU -1.9%. ALAB -1.6% on semi sector pressure.

bullets.title: Pre-market bright spots: INTC on CPU price hike, IONQ on quantum foundry, HOOD on prediction markets
bullets.body: INTC +4.6% on Northland upgrade citing PC CPU prices set to rise another 10% per Digitimes. IONQ +5.5% on midwest commercial foundry partnership for superconducting quantum devices. HOOD +3.4% selected as OG.com infrastructure partner for prediction markets; also partnering with Crypto.com to expand the platform. GLW +2.9% on multi-year, multi-billion-dollar Verizon fiber supply deal through 2032 covering 80M+ miles.

bullets.title: Corning-Verizon multi-billion fiber deal through 2032 anchors AI backbone buildout
bullets.body: Corning and Verizon signed a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar agreement for 80M+ miles of high-density optical fiber from 2027–2032, supporting Verizon's push to 40–50M broadband passings and hyperscaler AI backbone. Citi initiates GLW Buy at $220 PT (43% upside) applying 32x P/E to CY28 EPS, noting the agreement enables Corning to scale US manufacturing footprint.

bullets.title: September seasonality historically weakest month; macro setup (tariffs, yen vol, yields) adds caution
bullets.body: September averages -0.59% for the S&P 500 since 1940 and -1.10% in midterm years. Markets enter the week contending with Trump-era tariffs, Canada escalating with 15–50% levies on US goods, USD/JPY breaking below 155 (reviving carry-trade unwind fears), and Brent approaching $100. Treasury yields near highest since late 2023; 115 S&P 500 stocks now exhibit negative 6-month beta — far above prior peak of <80 from the dot-com era.

bullets.title: AI usage driving bifurcated market: AI Services basket +7.9% in two months; non-AI cyclicals lagging
bullets.body: 22V research notes an AI Usage Services basket up 7.9% over two months (+2.4% WoW), driven by lower rate sensitivity and strong EPS growth. Software names showing cash returns exceeding 100% of net income. Retail and Transports underperformed and are unlikely to recover without lower oil prices and inflation; Non-AI Cyclicals (Banks, Transports, Retailers) present valuation opportunity as Fed tightening risk rises.

bullets.title: Shopify -8.7% in Canada; BBD.B -6.2% on Trump comments; TSX -0.43%
bullets.body: S&P/TSX Composite fell 0.43% to 36,357. Shopify dropped 8.7% (C$183.31), Bombardier -6.2% on Trump tariff comments with sympathy selling in BRP -6.0%. Celestica bucked the trend, rising 3.1% to C$445.98. Base metals and energy broadly positive.

bullets.title: Hardware & Networking: improving CY27 fundamentals (+10% earnings) offset by multiple compression
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Hardware & Networking weekly notes C2Q26 earnings delivered CY27 revenue +7% and earnings +10% on average, but share prices are flat as multiples compressed. AI-levered companies show CY27 revenue +8%, earnings +16%, trading at 23x vs. 50%+ growth expectations. Companies combining earnings, revenue, and gross margin beats rewarded with +14% average share price gains; non-margin-beat cohort fell 6%.

bullets.title: Macro: Chile August CPI surprises at 0.62% m/m; JPM revises Dec forecast to 4.1%
bullets.body: Chile's August headline CPI came in at 0.62% m/m — well above JPM's 0.30% and consensus 0.2% — lifting the annual rate to 4.1% from 3.5%. Volatile components drove the beat: food +1.4% m/m and international airfares +32.6%. Seasonally adjusted 3-month annualized pace accelerated to 4.5% ar. Central Bank of Chile expected to hold policy rate unchanged.
